name: Cryptic crossword No 22,272
preamble: Those clues involving either (After 9) or (After 25) become either compound words or phrases prefixed by the stated answer. For example, the answer to 15 Across is a single word of eight letters while the answer to 3 Down is a hyphenated phrase containing three words of four, two and five letters each.

clue.text: Silly fellow grabbing ram

indicators.note: a word grabbing another clutches it in its middle, holding it inside

blocks.note: Sid is a stock man's name, standing for any chap
a tup is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Some foolish chap has seized hold of a ram.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid is a stock name for any fellow, and a tup is a ram in British farming dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and silly are plain synonyms, both describing foolish behaviour lacking sense.

clue.text: Good person, a laugher showing resilience

blocks.note: ST is short for saint
taken as written
mina is a variant spelling of mynah, the mimicking bird that can imitate laughter

explanation.surface: A cheerful saint whose good humour helps them bounce back.
explanation.walkthrough: A saint is the stock good person, giving ST; the mina (mynah) is a talking bird famed for copying human laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the capacity to endure and recover, which is resilience.

clue.text: Working for agreement, but lacking status

indicators.note: the agreement is lacking the status word, so that portion is removed from it

blocks.note: an understanding is an agreement
standing is one's status

explanation.surface: Someone toiling to get a deal, though they have little clout.
explanation.walkthrough: UNDERSTANDING minus STANDING leaves UNDER. Under means in the process of, as in under way or under construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under repair or under way is in operation or being worked on, so under can mean working.

clue.text: (After 9) Transferring affection, intimately bound together

blocks.note: handing something on is transferring it
love is fond affection

explanation.surface: Someone whose devotion has moved on to a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds HAND IN GLOVE; per the preamble the prefix HAND (9 across) is dropped and IN-GLOVE goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in glove describes a very close working relationship, often collusion, as snug as a hand inside its glove.

clue.text: Miserable article, thing written without love

indicators.note: written without love means the thing is spelt out minus that letter

blocks.note: the indefinite article
an object is a thing; written means it is spelt out in full
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A wretched little piece of writing, composed without any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as the letter O comes from tennis scoring, where love means nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a wretched, hopeless state, the same sense as utterly miserable.

clue.text: (After 25) Walker's crossing, female twisting boot on edge

indicators.note: the female is twisting the boot, so its letters are wrenched out of order

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the letters of boot rearranged
a ridge is a crest or edge

explanation.surface: A woman on a hiking path twists her boot on a precipice.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds FOOTBRIDGE; per the preamble the prefix FOOT (25 across) is dropped and BRIDGE goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge is a bridge for pedestrians only, so a crossing used by walkers.

clue.text: Old flame, frightful cat with head for precision

indicators.note: a frightful creature is a mess, so the animal's letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
the letters of cat rearranged
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A former lover with a scary cat and a sharp mind for detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a headland or promontory, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is accuracy and correctness down to fine detail, which is what precision means.

clue.text: (After 25) Pay former Labour leader to join TV programme

blocks.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party 1980-83
A long-running British police drama

explanation.surface: A politician is paid to appear on a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds FOOT THE BILL; per the preamble the prefix FOOT (25 across) is dropped and THE BILL goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To foot the bill is to settle the cost of something, an idiom meaning pay.

clue.text: Exceptionally grand repast that is included in summer celebrations

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order
the abbreviation is included in the meal, placed among its letters

blocks.note: taken as written, the main letters to rearrange
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An unusually lavish meal features at warm-weather festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: IE goes into GRAND REPAST before the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden parties are outdoor social gatherings typically held in the summer months, often with a grand spread.

clue.text: This and 25 may be completely together

definitions.text: This and 25 may be completely together

blocks.note: surface reading: two unknown items that might coexist somehow
setter's reading: an idiom for total restraint pairs this entry with 25 across

explanation.walkthrough: To be tied HAND and foot is to be bound completely; 25 is FOOT. Both words also prefix the themed answers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tied hand and foot means totally restrained, so the two body parts together express completeness.

clue.text: Expecting to go round building in which you'd find many a picture was drawn

indicators.note: the expecting word goes round the building, enclosing it in its middle

blocks.note: gravid means pregnant, expecting a baby

blocks.clueFragment: building in which you'd find many a picture
blocks.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman sets off around a gallery full of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is the London gallery; 'drawn' looks like it belongs with the pictures but means attracted.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to be pulled or attracted towards something, so gravitated matches was drawn in the passive sense.

clue.text: Bacterium against one wanting vigour

blocks.note: v is short for versus
the Roman numeral for one
brio is liveliness and spirit

explanation.surface: A germ opposed to anyone who lacks energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like a deletion signal but only places I next to BRIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrio is a genus of comma-shaped bacteria, including the one that causes cholera.

clue.text: Unpleasant person's meeting end in grass

blocks.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow; possessive gives the s
the tail is the end of something

explanation.surface: A nasty character comes to a sticky end in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog is slang for a despicable man.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog's-tail is a meadow grass, named for its spiky flower head resembling an animal's tail.

clue.text: Girl tucking into my old cake

indicators.note: the girl is tucking into the other word, pushing herself inside it

blocks.note: a girl's name
mine is the archaic form of my, used before a vowel

explanation.surface: A girl is eating my stale cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' suggests eating, which suits cake, but here it means going inside. 'Old' marks the archaic form of my.
explanation.definitionFit: A madeleine is a small shell-shaped French sponge, famous from Proust.

clue.text: English pride may spread? It used to at this time

definitions.text: It used to at this time

indicators.note: spread asks for the letters to be laid out afresh in a new arrangement

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether national pride may grow, as it once did on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is English pride, which used to spread at this time, when the imperial holiday was celebrated each May.
explanation.definitionFit: Empire Day, 24 May, was a British celebration of the Empire, a time when patriotic pride was expressed.

clue.text: (After 9) Little music maker with awful band in awful place

indicators.note: an awful group plays badly, so its letters are put out of tune and order
the band plays in the venue, so it sits inside that word

blocks.note: the letters of band rearranged
hell is the worst place imaginable

explanation.surface: A tiny instrument played by a terrible group in a dreadful venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds HANDBELL; per the preamble the prefix HAND (9 across) is dropped and BELL goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell rung by hand, so it is a little instrument making music.

clue.text: Silly person to opt for gym?

blocks.note: to do something is to go for it
PE is physical education, school gym

explanation.surface: Only a fool would choose to go to the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: DO plus PE; doing PE is opting for gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for an idiot, a stupid individual.

clue.text: Strange Roman way going into hollow

indicators.note: the road goes into the hollow, so it sits inside that word

blocks.note: a dent is a hollow
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: An odd Roman road that runs down into a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Via is the Latin for road, familiar from names like the Via Appia.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant means departing from the norm, so abnormal or odd in behaviour.

clue.text: Unfortunately, she's pally

indicators.note: unfortunately signals things have gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Regrettably, she is far too friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' does double duty: it is the definition and it also tells you the letters have gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Haplessly means without luck, an exact match for unfortunately as an adverb.

clue.text: (After 25) Base new lab term in physics unit

indicators.note: a new version of the words is made by remaking their letters

blocks.note: the foot of something is its base
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh laboratory word underpins a unit of physics.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds FOOT-LAMBERT; per the preamble the prefix FOOT (25 across) is dropped and LAMBERT goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The foot-lambert is an old imperial unit of luminance used in physics and photometry.

clue.text: It's despicable getting secret info

blocks.note: first meaning: mean and contemptible
second meaning: inside information on something

explanation.surface: It is shameful to obtain confidential intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-down is an adjective for base conduct, and the lowdown is a noun for the inside facts.

clue.text: (After 25) Stage illuminations excessively turned up in exits

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
the excess sits in the exits, placed within that word

blocks.note: too means excessively
flights are escapes

explanation.surface: Theatre lamps blazing far too brightly by the doors.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads the word bottom to top. The wordplay builds FOOTLIGHTS; per the preamble the prefix FOOT is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Footlights are the row of lamps along the front of a theatre stage, lighting the performers.

clue.text: (After 9) Deliver punch rapidly and successfully

blocks.note: to hand over is to deliver
a fist is a punch, as in a bunch of fives

explanation.surface: A boxer lands a blow quickly and effectively.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds HAND OVER FIST; per the preamble the prefix HAND (9 across) is dropped and OVER FIST goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Making money hand over fist means earning it quickly and in large amounts, so rapid success.

clue.text: (After 9) Who'd mend an awful second-hand item?

indicators.note: an awful job of mending leaves the words' letters in a mess

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Nobody would bother repairing such a shoddy used thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds HAND-ME-DOWN; per the preamble the prefix HAND (9 across) is dropped and ME-DOWN goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-me-down is clothing or goods passed on after an earlier owner has finished using them.

clue.text: Writer upset editor over environmental organisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

blocks.note: ed is short for editor
Friends of the Earth, a green campaign group

explanation.surface: An author annoys his editor about a green pressure group.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the reversed ED above FOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: It won't spread on bread? Bad luck!

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm cheese that cannot be smeared like a soft one
second meaning: a British exclamation of mock sympathy

explanation.walkthrough: Hard cheese! is British slang meaning tough luck, often said without much real sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a firm cheese that will not spread, and idiomatically a dismissive phrase meaning tough, too bad.

clue.text: This and 9 may be completely together

blocks.note: surface reading: two unknown items that might coexist somehow
setter's reading: an idiom for total restraint pairs 9 across with this entry

explanation.walkthrough: To be tied hand and FOOT is to be bound completely; 9 is HAND. Both words also prefix the themed answers.

clue.text: Your old flower lacking round inflorescence

indicators.note: the flower is lacking the round letter, so it is taken out

blocks.note: thy is the archaic form of your
a familiar flower
round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Your former bloom has lost its rounded flower head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks the archaic form of your; round stands for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A thyrse is a branched flower cluster, a panicle shaped like a bunch of grapes.

clue.text: Either side of river you'll find odd newts distributed

indicators.note: odd newts are strange ones, so their letters come out in a peculiar order
the letters lie on either side of the river, so they wrap around it

blocks.note: the letters of the amphibians rearranged
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Strange amphibians are scattered along both banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled NEWTS split around R: ST-R-EWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered about, the same as distributed or spread around.
